ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: small bedroom
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A snug bedroom for one: bed, bedside table, a light and a plant. Cheap enough to build several.

tips.li: Even a small private room beats a bed in the barracks: no snoring neighbors, no shared-bedroom penalty.
A cramped room drags impressiveness down. Build these early, then replace them with bigger rooms when you can.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: barracks
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Shared sleeping quarters for up to eight. Quick and cheap to build, and often the colony's first real shelter.

tips.li: Barracks are a fine start. As the colony grows richer, everyone expects more, and the shared-bedroom penalty starts to hurt.
People walking past sleepers wake them. Keep the barracks off the main corridors.
Couples want a double bed; two singles side by side don't count.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: prison cell
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A cell for one prisoner: a bed, a light, one door. Mark the bed "for prisoners" once it's built.

tips.li: Every extra door into a cell is another way out. Give each cell a single door and solid walls.
After it's built, select the bed and set it "for prisoners", or prisoners won't be taken there.
Fed, comfortable prisoners are easier to recruit. A light and a decent bed cost little.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: prison barracks
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A shared cell for up to four prisoners. Mark the beds "for prisoners" once they're built.

tips.li: When one prisoner breaks out, everyone in the same cell joins in. Several small cells are safer than one big one.
Keep prison cells away from your weapons and the storeroom.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: butcher's room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Butchering away from the stove: a butcher table and a light, ideally between the freezer and the kitchen.

tips.li: Butchering sprays blood. In its own room, the mess stays out of the kitchen, where it would raise the chance of food poisoning.
Put it right next to the freezer and the kitchen, so carcasses and meat travel as few steps as possible.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: brewery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A brewing bench and fermenting barrels for beer. Barrels only work between -1 °C and 32 °C.

tips.li: Fermenting barrels only work between -1 °C and 32 °C. An indoor room keeps them in range most of the year.
Beer counts as recreation and cheers people up, but too much leads to hangovers and, for some, alcohol addiction. Set a drug policy.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: heat shelter
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A room kept bearable in desert heat and heat waves without electricity: passive coolers and three beds.

tips.li: Passive coolers burn wood and can't cool below 17 °C. That won't keep food, but it keeps people out of heatstroke.
Coolers only help in a closed room. Keep the door shut and the walls thick.
No torches or campfires in here: they heat the room you're trying to cool.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: smithy
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two workbenches for weapons, armor and tools, and a light to work by.

tips.li: Workers walk for every ingredient. A shelf or stockpile right next to the bench saves hours every day.
A good floor and a light speed up work and keep the crafter happier.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: tailor's shop
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A tailoring bench, a shelf for cloth and leather, a light and a plant.

tips.li: Warm clothes widen the temperatures colonists can work in. Before winter, make parkas or tribalwear for everyone who goes outside.
Tattered clothes and clothes taken from the dead both sour moods. Keep a tailor busy making replacements.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: art studio
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A sculpting table, a light and a plant: somewhere for artists to make the colony beautiful.

tips.li: Sculptures can be moved wherever they're needed. A few good ones improve dining rooms, rec rooms and bedrooms alike, and they sell well.
Inspired artists make masterpieces. Keep an artist happy and give them time at the table.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: drug lab
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A drug lab bench and a light, for making medicine, recreational drugs or goods to trade.

tips.li: Drugs sell well and some are useful, but every colonist who takes them risks addiction. Set drug policies before you start production.
Penoxycyline prevents several diseases. It's worth making if your doctors keep fighting plague and malaria.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large hospital
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Four beds with two vitals monitors, a medicine shelf, a light and clean floors.

tips.li: Hospital beds and vitals monitors improve treatment and recovery. Sterile floors cut the risk of infection.
Build the hospital near the main entrance, so the wounded don't have to be carried across the whole base after a raid.
Keep medicine on a shelf inside the hospital so doctors don't walk to the storeroom mid-surgery.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: crematorium
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A crematorium and a light, for the dead you won't bury.

tips.li: Raiders' bodies lying around sour everyone's mood. Burn them, or at least drag them far away.
Put a corpse stockpile right outside, set to accept only corpses, so haulers bring the dead straight here.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: battery room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Three batteries under one roof, away from anything that burns.

tips.li: Batteries can short-circuit and start fires, especially when rain gets in. A roofed stone room keeps both problems contained.
Store enough to get through the night. Solar panels give nothing after dark.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: armory
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Shelves for weapons and armor, close to where the fighting happens.

tips.li: Keep weapons near your defensive line, not across the base, so fighters can arm themselves quickly when raiders arrive.
Never store weapons next to the prison. Escaped prisoners grab whatever weapons they find nearby.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: meditation room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A quiet room with a meditation spot, plants and soft light. Needs Royalty.

tips.li: Psycasters regain focus by meditating. Their focus types decide what helps: plants for natural, art for artistic, and so on.
Meditation also counts as recreation for everyone else.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: throne room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A throne facing the door, braziers on either side, music and space. Needs Royalty and a title.

tips.li: Nobles need a throne room that grows with their title: bigger, more impressive, and with more furnishings at every rank. Check the title's requirements in their info card.
A throne room only counts if nothing else is in it: no beds, no workbenches.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: classroom
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: School desks facing a blackboard, a toy box and a light. Needs Biotech and children.

tips.li: Children learn faster at school desks, and a blackboard in the same room helps more.
Kids need play too. A toy box nearby keeps them happy and learning.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: nursery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Cribs, a toy box, a light and a soft floor for the colony's youngest. Needs Biotech.

tips.li: Babies sleep a lot and cry when hungry. A nursery near the parents' rooms saves a lot of walking at night.
Keep the nursery warm and away from the entrance, where raiders come in.
